methodological_rigor.justification: The in vitro study uses established DLBCL cell lines (SU-DHL-8 and SU-DHL-10, with mention of SU-DHL-4, SU-DHL-6, DoHH2 although data are only shown for SU-DHL-8/10) and combines orthogonal readouts (CCK-8, trypan blue, DAPI/PI, western blot with nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation, immunofluorescence). The mechanistic logic is coherent: pan-caspase inhibitor Q-VD-OPh fails to rescue SU-DHL-10 but PARP-1 inhibitor olaparib does, with PAR accumulation and AIF/MIF nuclear translocation as parthanatos hallmarks. Weaknesses: all experiments are in cell lines only (no primary patient samples, no xenograft model), main findings center on a single cell line (SU-DHL-10), UVB is a proxy for radiotherapy with unclear clinical translatability, no PARP-1 genetic knockdown to confirm pharmacological findings, and sample size is 'at least three independent experiments' with one-way ANOVA but no power analysis.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical in vitro cell-line study with no animal or patient data, mapping to Oxford LoE 5 (mechanistic/basic science). Translational relevance is speculative: curcumin's poor bioavailability (<1%) is a major clinical hurdle the authors themselves acknowledge, and UVB is a weak analog for clinical radiotherapy for DLBCL. While identifying a novel cell-death mechanism (parthanatos) in DLBCL is mechanistically interesting, the path to clinical application is long and uncertain.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE is the closest applicable standard for preclinical studies, though this study has no animal work; ARRIVE elements still apply to cell-line research. Core methods items are described: cell line sources, reagent catalog numbers, culture conditions, protein amounts, antibody dilutions, and statistical tests. Gaps: cell line authentication (STR profiling) is not mentioned, mycoplasma testing not reported, blinding of western/imaging quantification not stated, and the methods section includes overly verbose general procedures (cell thawing, BCA) with less detail on specific experimental conditions (e.g., UVB doses rationalization). No data availability statement; western blot uncropped blots and numerical source data not indicated as deposited.

novelty_literature.justification: The authors claim this is 'the first report demonstrating curcumin-induced activation of the parthanatos pathway in DLBCL cells,' extending prior parthanatos work from neurodegeneration, leukemia, myeloma, prostate cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma into DLBCL. Combining curcumin with UVB as a radiosensitization model via parthanatos is a novel mechanistic angle. While curcumin's anticancer effects and parthanatos generally are established, this specific combination in DLBCL is new. Guarding against novelty leniency: novelty is bounded by single cell line and absence of in vivo validation, but the first-in-disease mechanistic demonstration is reasonable.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is organized and the figure legends are described. However, writing issues include: redundant phrasing ('Curcumin, a natural polyphenol, curcumin has garnered...'), repeated wording ('upon its nuclear translocation leading to cell death'), a description of preliminary data as 'data not shown', and some methods sections (cell thawing, BCA assay, passaging) are overly generic and could be shortened. Reference 68 is cited both for curcumin protecting skin from UVB and for SU-DHL-10 lacking BAX expression, which is implausible and likely a citation error. Reference 32 is miscited: Wang 2009 is the canonical parthanatos description but the listed reference is a 2022 CNS Neurosci Ther paper. Readable overall but needs editorial review.

key_strengths: First report of curcumin-induced parthanatos in DLBCL, identifying a caspase-independent cell-death mechanism relevant to apoptosis-resistant double-hit lymphoma (SU-DHL-10)
Orthogonal experimental readouts (CCK-8, trypan blue, DAPI/PI, nuclear/cytoplasmic western blot, immunofluorescence) converge on PARP-1/AIF/MIF activation
Pharmacological dissection with Q-VD-OPh (pan-caspase) and olaparib (PARP-1 inhibitor) provides mechanism-level evidence that curcumin acts via PARP-1-dependent parthanatos
Demonstrates synergy between low-dose curcumin and UVB as a radiosensitization proxy, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy
key_concerns: Findings are based almost entirely on a single cell line (SU-DHL-10), with no primary patient samples, patient-derived xenografts, or in vivo work
UVB is a weak analog for clinical radiotherapy; translational implications for DLBCL radiotherapy remain speculative
Curcumin's very low oral bioavailability (<1%) is acknowledged but the paper offers no formulation or PK data to address this translational gap
Cell line authentication, mycoplasma testing, and blinding of quantification not reported; methods include verbose generic protocols while lacking detail on UVB dosing rationale
Apparent reference mis-citation (ref 68 cited for two unrelated claims; ref 32 appears to cite a 2022 paper when a 2009 foundational parthanatos paper is described)
No genetic loss-of-function confirmation (PARP-1 siRNA/CRISPR) to complement pharmacological inhibition
chief_reviewer.rationale: A mechanistically interesting but preclinical-only in vitro study restricted to one cell line. Apparent reference mis-citations raise concerns about possibly fabricated supporting claims, though not central to the core data. Tier 3 is the highest plausible venue with major revisions to validate in additional DLBCL subtypes and in vivo models and to correct reference errors.
